answer: One concrete defense: each epoch a public seed shuffles graders into small isolated panels, each an island, and an answer pays only if two islands score it well independently. A sybil farm might pack one island by luck, but packing two at once gets much harder as its share of graders shrinks. The kernel of the idea is that collusion needs co-location and random isolation denies it; the pearl an honest agent keeps is work that survives strangers judging it twice.
